# 1 Maccabees Chapter 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 16 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_016_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And John went up from Gazara and reported to Simon his father what Cendebaeus had done.

**2** And Simon called his two older sons Judas and John, and said to them: "I and my brothers and my father's house have fought the wars of Israel from our youth until this day, and things have prospered in our hands to deliver Israel many times.

**3** But now I have grown old, and you by his mercy are of mature age. Take my place and my brother's place and go out and fight for our nation, and let the help from heaven be with you."

**4** And he chose from the country twenty thousand men of war and cavalry, and they marched against Cendebaeus and slept in Modein.

**5** And they arose in the morning and went into the plain, and behold, a great army came to meet them, both infantry and cavalry, and between them was a torrent.

**6** And John and his people drew near opposite them for battle. And he saw that the people were afraid to cross the torrent, and he crossed first, and the men saw it and crossed after him.

**7** And he divided the people and put the cavalry in the midst of the infantry, for the cavalry of the enemy was very numerous.

**8** And they sounded the trumpets, and Cendebaeus was routed and many of his men fell wounded, and the rest fled into the stronghold.

**9** And Judas the brother of John was wounded at that time, but John pursued them until he came to Kidron which Cendebaeus had built.

**10** And they fled into the towers that were in the fields of Azotus, and he burned it with fire, and about two thousand of them fell, and he returned to Judea in peace.

**11** Now Ptolemy son of Abubus had been appointed commander over the plain of Jericho, and he had much silver and gold,

**12** for he was son-in-law to the high priest.

**13** And his heart was lifted up and he purposed to get possession of the country, and he dealt treacherously with Simon and his sons to destroy them.

**14** Now Simon was visiting the cities of the country and looking after their welfare, and he went down to Jericho, he and his sons Mattathias and Judas, in the one hundred and seventy-seventh year, in the eleventh month — that is, the month of Shebat.

**15** And the son of Abubus received them with treachery into the little stronghold called Dok that he had built, and he made them a great banquet, and hid men there.

**16** And when Simon and his sons had become drunk with wine, Ptolemy and his men rose up and took their weapons and came upon Simon in the banquet hall and killed him and his two sons and some of his servants.

**17** And he committed a great act of treachery and returned evil for good.

**18** And Ptolemy wrote these things and sent to the king that he should send him troops to help him and that he should give over to him their country and their cities.

**19** And he sent others to Gazara to kill John; and to the commanders of thousands he sent letters to come to him that he might give them silver and gold and gifts.

**20** And he sent others to seize Jerusalem and the hill of the temple.

**21** And someone ran ahead and reported to John at Gazara that his father and his brothers had perished, and that "he has sent men to kill you also."

**22** And when he heard this, he was greatly shocked, and he seized the men who came to kill him and killed them, for he knew that they sought to kill him.

**23** And the rest of the acts of John and his wars and his valiant deeds that he did, and the building of the walls that he built, and his achievements —

**24** behold, these are written in the annals of his high priesthood, from the time when he became high priest after his father.
